lines.text: Should your laptop stay plugged in all day? Most people think it kills the battery.
Batteries do wear out. They age fastest when they sit full at a hundred percent, and when they get hot.
But modern laptops stop charging when they're full. Then the charger runs the laptop, and the battery rests.
Many also hold the charge near eighty percent, so the battery doesn't sit full all day.
On a Mac, that's Optimized Battery Charging, or a charge limit. Dell's Power Manager has a setting too.
The real enemy is heat. Don't charge it on a bed or a pillow, where the vents get blocked.
Plug it in, turn on the limit, keep it cool. That's the plugged-in myth.

post.title: Should your laptop stay plugged in?
post.caption:
Should your laptop stay plugged in all day? 🔌 Mostly a myth that it kills the battery.

Lithium-ion batteries age fastest when they sit full at 100% and when they get hot. But modern laptops stop charging when they're full, and then the charger runs the laptop. Many also hold the charge near 80%: on a Mac, Optimized Battery Charging learns your routine and waits past 80%, and Apple silicon Macs on macOS Tahoe 26.4 or later have a Charge Limit you can set from 80 to 100%. Dell Power Manager has a Primarily AC Use mode and a Custom start / stop setting for the same job. The real enemy is heat: don't charge it on a bed or a pillow, where the vents are blocked.

Plug it in, turn on the limit, keep it cool. Send this to the friend who unplugs their laptop every hour.
keywords: should i keep my laptop plugged in

sources.note: Apple Support, About Optimized Battery Charging and Charge Limit on Mac: Optimized Battery Charging uses on-device learning to delay charging past 80% when it expects a long time on power; Charge Limit (Apple silicon, macOS Tahoe 26.4 or later) from 80% to 100%; the Mac charges to 100% now and then to keep its estimate accurate (read 18 Nov 2026).

Dell Power Manager User's Guide, Battery settings: Primarily AC Use lowers the charge threshold to extend battery life for systems that mostly run plugged in; Custom sets start and stop thresholds (read 18 Nov 2026).

Apple, Batteries: Maximizing Performance: avoid ambient temperatures above 35 °C (95 °F), which can permanently damage battery capacity; charging in heat makes it worse (read 18 Nov 2026). Apple Support 102589, battery health management on Apple silicon: it watches the battery's temperature history and charging patterns to slow chemical ageing.
